evidence.quote:
"""DCGAN training: two networks, two optimisers, one batch loop.

The ordering that looks wrong to a linter and is right to a practitioner:
`opt_d.step()` genuinely precedes `loss_g.backward()`, because they belong to
two different optimisation problems.
"""
from models import LATENT_DIM, Discriminator, Generator, weights_init

DATA_ROOT = "data/celeba"
SEED = 999
EPOCHS = 25
BATCH_SIZE = 128
WORKERS = 4
LR = 2e-4
BETAS = (0.5, 0.999)
SAMPLE_DIR = "samples"

def train(epochs: int = EPOCHS) -> tuple:
    seed_everything()
    device = pick_device()
    loader = build_loader()

    netG = Generator().to(device)
    netD = Discriminator().to(device)
    netG.apply(weights_init)
    netD.apply(weights_init)

criterion = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
    opt_g = torch.optim.Adam(netG.parameters(), lr=LR, betas=BETAS)
    opt_d = torch.optim.Adam(netD.parameters(), lr=LR, betas=BETAS)

fixed_noise = torch.randn(64, LATENT_DIM, 1, 1, device=device)
    d_running = 0.0
    g_running = 0.0

# --- discriminator: maximise log D(x) + log(1 - D(G(z)))
            opt_d.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            logits_real = netD(real_images)
            loss_real = criterion(logits_real, real_labels)

noise = torch.randn(batch, LATENT_DIM, 1, 1, device=device)
            fake_images = netG(noise)
            logits_fake = netD(fake_images.detach())
            loss_fake = criterion(logits_fake, fake_labels)
            loss_d = loss_real + loss_fake

# --- generator: maximise log D(G(z))
            opt_g.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            logits_for_g = netD(fake_images)
            loss_g = criterion(logits_for_g, real_labels)
            loss_g.backward()
            opt_g.step()

d_running += loss_d.item()
            g_running += loss_g.item()
            if step % 100 == 0:
                print("epoch %d step %d loss_d %.4f loss_g %.4f"
                      % (epoch, step, loss_d.item(), loss_g.item()))

sample_grid(netG, fixed_noise, epoch)
        torch.save({"netG": netG.state_dict(), "netD": netD.state_dict()},
                   "dcgan_epoch%d.pt" % epoch)

@torch.no_grad()
def sample_grid(netG, noise: torch.Tensor, epoch: int) -> str:
    """Write a fixed-noise grid so the run can be watched frame by frame."""
    netG.eval()
    images = netG(noise)
    path = "%s/epoch_%03d.png" % (SAMPLE_DIR, epoch)
    save_image(images * 0.5 + 0.5, path, nrow=8)
    netG.train()

findings.message: The generator phase backpropagates through netD without any visible discriminator freeze. Under standard trainable-module semantics, this accumulates D gradients on top of the prior D gradients, yet opt_g targets only G. The next batch clears D before its next backward, so this is not an extra D update; it is primarily a potential compute and gradient-buffer inefficiency.
findings.suggestion: If profiling shows this matters, temporarily disable D parameter gradients during the generator phase while preserving the input-gradient path through D, then restore them before the next discriminator phase. Confirm the imported model's parameter settings first.
findings.title: Generator backward likely computes discriminator gradients that are not stepped

nodes.detail: Seeds Python, NumPy, and Torch; selects CUDA when available, otherwise CPU; and constructs a transformed ImageFolder loader with shuffle and drop_last enabled.
nodes.label: Seed, choose device, and build shuffled loader

nodes.detail: Creates Generator and Discriminator instances, moves both to the selected device, and applies the imported weights_init function. Their internal architectures are outside the inspected workspace source.
nodes.label: Construct and initialize G and D

nodes.detail: The shared criterion is BCEWithLogitsLoss. opt_g is constructed only from netG.parameters(); opt_d is constructed only from netD.parameters(). Consequently, each optimizer step can update only its own registered parameter set.
nodes.label: Bind BCE-with-logits loss and separate Adam targets

nodes.detail: For every loader batch, real_images move to the device; real_labels is an all-one vector and fake_labels is an all-zero vector sized from the actual batch.
nodes.label: Enter nested epoch/batch loops and make 1/0 targets

nodes.detail: After clearing discriminator gradients, real images pass through netD and loss_real compares the resulting logits with real (one) labels. Under normal autograd semantics this branch contributes gradients to D, not to any generator parameters.
nodes.label: Real branch: D(x) → BCE(logits, 1)

nodes.detail: Fresh latent noise is sampled and sent through netG once. The original fake_images tensor retains its generator autograd history for the later generator phase.
nodes.label: Sample z and synthesize fake_images = G(z)

nodes.detail: netD receives fake_images.detach() for loss_fake. The detached view shares values with fake_images but severs this discriminator-loss path back into G; the original non-detached fake_images remains available.
nodes.label: Detach only the fake tensor fed to the D loss

nodes.detail: The discriminator classifies detached generated images and loss_fake compares those logits with fake (zero) labels. This supplies a fake-classification gradient to D while the detach boundary blocks a gradient to G.
nodes.label: Fake branch: D(stopgrad(G(z))) → BCE(logits, 0)

nodes.detail: The two BCE terms are summed and one backward call accumulates their gradients on discriminator parameters. The fake branch cannot continue into G because its D input was detached.
nodes.label: L_D = L_real + L_fake; backpropagate both D branches

nodes.detail: The discriminator optimizer steps immediately after loss_d.backward(). Because opt_d was built from netD.parameters(), this is the only parameter set it targets. The step intentionally precedes the generator backward because the two losses belong to separate optimization problems.
nodes.label: opt_d.step() updates only discriminator parameters

nodes.detail: opt_g.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) removes generator gradients left from the preceding batch. It does not destroy the autograd history already attached to fake_images.
nodes.label: Clear generator gradients after the D step

nodes.detail: The same original fake_images—not its detached view—is passed through netD after opt_d.step(). Thus the generator loss is evaluated through the discriminator parameters just updated in this batch, with a connected path from D's output back through fake_images to G.
nodes.label: Reuse non-detached fake_images through updated D

nodes.detail: Generated images are deliberately paired with real (one) targets. Minimizing this BCE-with-logits loss is the non-saturating objective that encourages G to make D score its samples as real, matching the source comment's maximize log D(G(z)).
nodes.label: L_G = BCE(D(G(z)), 1)

nodes.detail: loss_g.backward() follows the connected path loss_g → logits_for_g → netD → fake_images → netG. Assuming the imported D parameters retain normal requires_grad=True, this backward also accumulates discriminator gradients, but opt_g.step() can update only netG.parameters(). Those D gradients are not stepped and are cleared by opt_d.zero_grad at the next batch start.
nodes.label: Backpropagate through D into G; step only G

nodes.detail: Scalar loss values are accumulated and every 100 steps they are printed. Control returns to the inner loader loop, so each subsequent batch repeats the same discriminator-first, generator-second alternation.
nodes.label: Accumulate/report losses, then repeat D → G for next batch

nodes.detail: When the inner batch loop ends, sample_grid runs netG under no_grad in evaluation mode using fixed noise, writes an image grid, restores train mode, and the caller saves both model state dictionaries. The outer epoch loop then begins the next batch cycle if epochs remain.
nodes.label: After each epoch, render fixed-noise samples and checkpoint G/D
